body.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_W\), \(P\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat\Sigma_{zz,n})<m_{\Sigma}/2\}=O(n^{-2})\). On the complementary event, \(\|R_n(\widehat\Sigma_{zz,n})-\widehat\Sigma_{zz,n}^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq4n^{-2}/m_{\Sigma}^2\); consequently the ridge-totalized reduced forms, score, estimated influence process, and multiplier critical value differ from their inverse-defined versions by \(o_P(n^{-1/2})\) uniformly. Thus the near-singular fallback event is asymptotically immaterial for every stated weak limit and, because confidence sets lie in compact \(K\), for the stated expected outer-loss rates.
body.justification: The lemma makes all reported procedures measurable on singular samples while preserving their first-order contact and interior behavior.
body.gap: Watson et al.'s implementation removes undefined rows; this result replaces that implicit conditioning by an every-sample convention and quantifies its uniform asymptotic cost.
body.consumer: Software can return an interval or confidence hull on every dataset without altering the endpoint laws, coverage claim, or adaptive loss frontier.
